newsitem.title: USA: US meat groups expecting WTO to rule against EU.
newsitem.headline: US meat groups expecting WTO to rule against EU.

text.p: U.S. meat industry groups were eagerly anticipating the release of a World Trade Organization interim report Wednesday that was expected to rule in favor of the U.S. complaint against the European Union's ban on imports of hormone-treated beef.
"We're hearing that it's likely to be favorable for the United States," said Chuck Lambert of the National Cattlemen's Beef Association.
The WTO report on the decade-old dispute is expected to be released, on a confidential basis, to the U.S. Trade Representive's office at midday Wednesday, a USTR spokesperson said.
"We're supposed to get the report by noon," said Kirsten Powers. "But the interim reports are confidential...we don't talk about them."

European Union imposed a ban on beef treated with growth hormones in 1989. Since that time, U.S. beef exports to the EU have plunged to only around $30 million worth from over $140 million worth in 1988.
Washington has charged that hormones have been proven to be safe, and that the EU measures were not based on sound science, but a move to block access to the European market.
The U.S. meat industry said a decision in favor of the United States would be a "very big deal" and would mean a significant increase in U.S. meat shipments to Europe.
Lambert said the United STates is losing anywhere from $250 million to half a billion dollars worth of beef trade to the EU as a result of the ban.

Prior to the ban, U.S. beef shipments to Europe were averaging at least $100 million per year. Lambert said that the $100 million of business would "easily" have grown to at least $250 worth during the years of the ban.
After the WTO releases its interim report, there is a period of about 45 days in which parties to the case review the report before the final report is issues.

Final reports are generally identical to the interim reports. Parties have a number of options after the final ruling -- changes can be implemented according to prescribed WTO recommendations, compensation can be paid to the injured nation, or the ruling can be appealed.
